content.content:
Criteria for this edge, applied to the dependent's recorded decision read against the decision this edge's prerequisite records; nothing runs, and no surface, rendering, pointer or DOM state is probed.

(1) Subject. A node whose recorded content is still a placeholder, or otherwise states no commitment, leaves the check with no subject to read: that absence is a finding, named as such. It is a finding for the prerequisite as much as for the dependent when the check reads the dependent against it.

(2) Licence. No element of the dependent contradicts the prerequisite. Fail on every contradicting element, naming the element and the part of the prerequisite it contradicts: an element that forbids, reverses, replaces or withholds an outcome the prerequisite fixes, or that narrows the prerequisite by excepting a case it covers. The contradiction this clause looks for is an element that re-decides a presentation instead of adding a state to it — one that makes a presentation the prerequisite fixes conditional, temporary or dependent on further input, that shows that presentation only while the dependent's own state holds, or that presents the dependent's state as the thing which establishes what the entry is. An element that adds a state to an entry whose presentation the prerequisite settled, and leaves that settled presentation as it is whenever the added state does not hold, stays inside the licence.

(3) Grounding. The check presumes no element of the dependent and no particular clause of the prerequisite; which element is at issue is a finding named only in the check's output. It requires no wording, sentence order or vocabulary of the dependent, restates no dependent, and invents no rule the prerequisite does not state.

(4) Decidability. A reviewer must be able to finish this check with one of two answers — a named contradicting element, or the statement that there is none — without supplying a rule neither recorded node states. If neither answer is reachable from the recorded statements alone, that is a finding.
content.rationale:
Both endpoints are inline prose commitments: the prerequisite is a recorded decision about how a ref-path entry is presented, and the dependent is a commitment in words, so this edge sits in the evaluation matrix's natural-to-natural cell, evals/natural-to-natural.md, and takes the gate form — non-contradiction, applied by reading the two recorded nodes. The strictness rule puts it no higher: children of the natural layer are commitments in words, and an evaluation over such a child checks non-violation and never demands behaviour, so asking a surface to render an entry, react to a pointer or exist as code would probe observables the child's layer does not carry and would presuppose a code-layer decision this edge does not record. Nothing is run for that reason; content.ref is inline because the criterion itself is the whole check.

What the criterion has to catch here is narrower than the dependent's whole subject. The dependent adds a state to an entry whose presentation the prerequisite already settles, and the licence is used soundly only while that presentation is left where the prerequisite put it and the added state is a state of it rather than a substitute for it. A dependent that made the presentation conditional on its own state, that showed the presentation only while that state held, or that restated the presentation as its own decision would be borrowing the prerequisite's subject instead of using it, and would do so without naming it — clause (2) is written to find exactly that, in whichever element the reviewer's read turns up, rather than to police the prose.

Every clause is decidable from the recorded statements, names nothing endpoint-specific in advance, demands no wording of the dependent and survives the dependent being rewritten without changing what it decides. Clause (1) keeps the check honest while a node is still a skeleton: a placeholder yields no subject to read, and that is a finding the check names rather than a silent pass.
